stories.title: Coldcard exploit reignites hardware-wallet security debate
stories.summary: A newly disclosed exploit targeting Coldcard hardware wallets has put self-custody security back in the spotlight. Cointelegraph examined whether the attacks mean hardware wallets broadly are now insecure, while CoinDesk reported analysts suggesting the scare could push some investors toward regulated bitcoin products instead of self-custody.
stories.whyItMatters: Confidence in self-custody tools underpins how much bitcoin sits outside exchanges and ETFs, so a credible hardware-wallet exploit can shift both behavior and flows.
whatToWatch: Any official response or patch from Coldcard
Whether other hardware wallet makers report similar vulnerabilities
ETF flow data in the days following the disclosure
questions: What exactly is the scope and mechanism of the exploit?
Has Coldcard confirmed which devices or firmware versions are affected?

sources.title: Coldcard exploit could boost demand for regulated bitcoin exposure, analysts say
Do the Coldcard attacks mean all hardware wallets are now insecure?

stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs snap back with inflows after cold-wallet hack stokes custody worries
stories.summary: Bitcoin ETFs logged fresh inflows even as a cold-wallet hack reignited debate over custody security, according to Cointelegraph. CryptoSlate reported the rebound was notable given a prior single-day exit of about $265 million across Bitcoin ETFs, with seven funds bouncing back together.
stories.whyItMatters: Sharp reversals in ETF flows are one of the clearest real-time gauges of institutional sentiment toward bitcoin.
whatToWatch: Whether inflows persist in the next reporting period
Any disclosed link between the mass exit and the custody incident
questions: What specifically triggered the earlier $265 million outflow?
Is the rebound tied to the hardware-wallet exploit story or a separate driver?

stories.title: Bitcoin and broader crypto market lag as global equities hit record highs
stories.summary: Bitcoin and the wider crypto market failed to keep pace with global equities as stock indices set fresh records, CoinDesk reported. Separately, CryptoSlate highlighted one piece of crypto-adjacent corporate activity: a cellular chipmaker sold roughly 1,200 bitcoin, using the proceeds to erase its debt and double its cash position.
stories.whyItMatters: A widening gap between crypto and equity performance raises questions about bitcoin's current role as a risk asset versus a hedge, and corporate treasury sales add supply-side context.
whatToWatch: Whether the performance gap between bitcoin and equities widens or narrows
Any further corporate treasury bitcoin sales
questions: Which chipmaker sold the bitcoin, and why now?
Is the equities-crypto divergence a rotation or a broader risk-off signal for crypto?

stories.title: BlackRock's ETHA reverse split set to sharply cut Ethereum trading costs
stories.summary: BlackRock is carrying out a reverse split of its spot Ether ETF, ETHA, which CryptoSlate reports will make trading the fund far cheaper per unit than buying ETH directly through Coinbase. The move restructures share pricing without changing the fund's underlying holdings.
stories.whyItMatters: Lower effective trading costs on a major spot ETH ETF could pull more volume away from direct exchange purchases and toward regulated wrappers.
whatToWatch: The effective date of the reverse split
ETHA trading volume and flows following the change
questions: What prompted BlackRock to pursue a reverse split now?
Will other ETH ETF issuers follow with similar share restructurings?

stories.title: Bitcoin holds flat near $64,000 as stocks hit records on Hormuz reopening hopes
stories.summary: Bitcoin traded roughly flat around $64,000 even as stock markets printed fresh records, with CoinDesk and Cointelegraph both citing progress toward a Hormuz Strait reopening deal as a driver of broader risk appetite. Cointelegraph noted the S&P 500's advance pushed its market cap to a reported $70 trillion.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin's failure to rally alongside easing geopolitical risk and record equities tests the narrative that it trades as a macro risk-on asset.
whatToWatch: Finalization of the Hormuz reopening deal
Bitcoin's price reaction if the deal is confirmed
questions: What are the actual terms and timeline of the Hormuz deal?
Why has bitcoin decoupled from the equity rally?

stories.title: Crypto whales are accumulating as bear market nears late stage, CryptoQuant says
stories.summary: On-chain analytics firm CryptoQuant said large crypto holders are accumulating, a pattern it associates with the later stages of a bear market, according to Cointelegraph. The report frames current whale behavior as a potential inflection signal rather than a confirmed trend reversal.
stories.whyItMatters: Whale accumulation is closely watched as a leading indicator, though it's a probabilistic signal, not a guarantee of a market turn.
whatToWatch: Follow-up on-chain data confirming or reversing the accumulation trend
Price action in the weeks following the report
questions: What time frame and wallet thresholds define "whale" accumulation here?
How reliable has this indicator been in past cycles?

stories.title: Proposed 54% cut to Ethereum staking rewards could break popular DeFi leverage loop
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reported that a proposed 54% reduction in Ethereum staking rewards could turn a widely used leveraged-staking strategy in DeFi from a yield play into a daily loss maker. The concern centers on strategies that borrow against staked ETH to amplify returns, which depend on rewards outpacing borrowing costs.
stories.whyItMatters: Changes to staking yield ripple through DeFi leverage products, and a reward cut steep enough to flip a popular strategy negative could trigger unwinding across protocols.
whatToWatch: Progress of the proposal through Ethereum's governance process
Whether DeFi protocols adjust or wind down affected leverage products preemptively
questions: Which specific proposal is driving this, and what's its timeline?
How much capital is currently deployed in the affected leverage strategy?

stories.title: Strive's 20 BTC purchase came with dilution that cut shareholders' bitcoin exposure
stories.summary: Bitcoin treasury company Strive bought 20 BTC, but CryptoSlate reported the purchase was funded alongside the issuance of 110,000 new shares, which left existing shareholders with less bitcoin exposure per share than before. The report frames the deal as a case where a headline bitcoin purchase masked net dilution.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a concrete illustration of the dilution risk embedded in equity-financed bitcoin treasury strategies, a model several public companies now use.
whatToWatch: Whether Strive makes further purchases financed by additional share issuance
Trends in bitcoin-per-share, the metric investors use to judge these treasury vehicles
questions: Why did Strive choose to fund this purchase via new shares rather than cash on hand?
Does Strive plan further capital raises tied to bitcoin accumulation?

stories.title: Ondo Finance hires former Blockchain.com CFO Adam Schlisman
stories.summary: Tokenization platform Ondo Finance has hired Adam Schlisman, the former chief financial officer of Blockchain.com, according to CoinDesk. No further details on his mandate at Ondo were reported.
stories.whyItMatters: Senior finance hires from established crypto firms signal continued institutional buildout in the tokenized real-world-asset sector.
whatToWatch: Schlisman's specific role and priorities at Ondo
Further executive hires as Ondo scales
questions: What prompted his departure from Blockchain.com?
What near-term initiatives will he lead at Ondo?

stories.title: SpaceX shares extend decline to 11% on lockup expiration and capex concerns
stories.summary: SpaceX shares extended losses to an 11% decline, CoinDesk reported, attributing the drop to a lockup expiration freeing up shares for sale alongside investor concerns about the company's capital expenditure spending.
stories.whyItMatters: Large moves in major private/tech names are tracked by the same institutional and venture investor base active in crypto markets, making them a relevant cross-market signal.
whatToWatch: Whether the decline continues as lockup shares are sold
Any company commentary addressing capex spending concerns
questions: How large is the lockup expiration relative to total shares outstanding?
What specific capex plans are driving investor concern?

stories.title: Ethereum proposal would zero out staking rewards once half of ETH supply is staked
stories.summary: Decrypt reported on an Ethereum proposal that would reduce staking rewards to zero if the share of ETH staked reaches 50% of supply, a mechanism intended to cap how much ETH gets locked into staking. The proposal is a policy change under discussion rather than a confirmed protocol update.
stories.whyItMatters: Staking-ratio caps would reshape ETH supply dynamics, validator economics, and the incentives behind liquid-staking and leverage products built on top of staking yield.
whatToWatch: Discussion and potential vote on the proposal within Ethereum's governance process
The current trajectory of the total ETH staking ratio
questions: Who put forward this proposal and how much support does it have?
How close is the current staked share to the 50% threshold?

sources.title: Ethereum Proposal Would Burn Staking Rewards to Zero if Half of ETH Is Staked

stories.title: Circle shares fall 3% on revenue miss despite beating earnings expectations
stories.summary: Circle shares dropped about 3% after the stablecoin issuer reported earnings that beat expectations but revenue that fell short, according to CoinDesk. The mixed results suggest cost or margin dynamics offset top-line softness.
stories.whyItMatters: As the issuer of USDC, Circle's financial results serve as a bellwether for stablecoin economics and issuer profitability more broadly.
whatToWatch: Management commentary or guidance addressing the revenue miss
USDC circulation and market-share trends in coming quarters
questions: What specifically drove the revenue shortfall?
Does the miss reflect competitive pressure on stablecoin market share?
